title: Exact vector Akhmediev breathers dominated by a linearly stable frequency
authors: Wen-Rong Sun, Chong Liu, Lei Wang, Fabio Baronio
abstract: In the scalar nonlinear Schrodinger equation, an Akhmediev breather (AB) is dominated by a frequency that lies inside the modulation instability gain band. This exactly correspondence between instability and breathers is challenged in vector systems such as the Manakov system, where the gain spectrum splits into disconnected lobes separated by stable gaps. We analytically and numerically construct an AB that is generated by unstable modes but is spectrally dominated by a stable harmonic at its peak. Numerical simulations starting from a simple continuous wave background perturbed only by the unstable harmonics confirm that the stable component emerges spontaneously and becomes dominant without any initial seed. We identify the precise parameter window in which this phenomenon occurs and show that this passive amplification of the linearly stable component is driven by four-wave mixing, which accounts for 96% of the nonlinear forcing. Given the universality of the Manakov system across nonlinear physics, from nonlinear optics to ultracold quantum gases, these results open an experimentally accessible new perspective on breather dynamics, one in which linearly stable frequencies can dominate.
summary: This paper analyzes Akhmediev breathers in the Manakov system, challenging the assumption that breather spectra must be governed by linearly unstable modes. Through numerical simulation and detailed analysis of nonlinear forcing, the authors prove that a spectrally stable harmonic can spontaneously become dominant at the breather's peak. This mechanism is driven purely by four-wave mixing, offering new insights into nonlinear wave dynamics across various physical platforms.
main_problem: The study investigates whether an Akhmediev breather (AB) can be spectrally dominated by a frequency component that is linearly stable, contrary to the usual expectation derived from modulation instability theory.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that in the Manakov system, a stable harmonic component ($n=\pm 2$) can spontaneously emerge and dominate the spectrum of an AB peak, driven entirely by four-wave mixing from initially unstable modes.
method: The analysis combines linear stability theory (calculating MI gain) with numerical simulations using the Manakov equation to track spectral energy distribution over time.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the Manakov nonlinear Schrödinger equation, governing two coupled wave components ($\psi^{(1)}, \psi^{(2)}$). The analysis focuses on constructing and simulating a third-order Akhmediev breather solution.
key_observables: Dominance measure $D(j)$ (quantifying stable harmonic contribution), Fourier amplitudes $|A_n|$, and the nonlinear forcing term derived from four-wave mixing.
important_parameters: The wavenumber offset $ eta$ is critical, with a specific window ($1 \le  eta < 1.5$) identified where this spectral dominance occurs.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of the Manakov system description and relies on isolating the nonlinear forcing term to quantify its source (four-wave mixing).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition of the dominance measure $D(j)$ towards unity for specific parameters, show the time evolution of Fourier amplitudes peaking at stable harmonics, and confirm that four-wave mixing accounts for most of the nonlinear driving.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical conflict (stable vs. unstable spectral control) to constructing the AB solution, performing linear stability analysis, running numerical simulations on the Manakov system, and finally quantifying the mechanism via nonlinear forcing analysis.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete example of how strong nonlinearity can fundamentally alter the spectral dynamics of wave packets, suggesting that energy transfer mechanisms (like four-wave mixing) can overcome linear stability constraints in physical systems relevant to quantum optics and Bose-Einstein condensates.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Gain curves G(n, β) of the ﬁrst three modulation harmonics (n = 1, 2, 3) for the focusing Manakov system with a = 1 and ω = 1. The second harmonic (n = 2) becomes linearly stable (gain zero) for β ≥1, while the ﬁrst (n = 1) and third (n = 3) harmonics remain unstable in the shaded window 1 ≤β < 1.5. This window, where unstable modes alternate with a stable one, is the parameter range explored in this work.

FIG. 2. Dominance D(j) of the n = ±2 sideband at the peak of the third-order Akhmediev breather as a function of β. The blue solid (red dashed) line represents the ψ(1) (ψ(2)) component. The green shaded area marks the parameter in- terval where both polarizations are simultaneously dominated by the linearly stable 2ω harmonic (D ≈1).

FIG. 5. Discrete Fourier amplitudes |A(1) n | (left) and |A(2) n | (right) at the peak of the third-order Akhmediev breather for β = 1.44. In both polarization components, the n = ±2 harmonic dominates the spectrum despite being linearly stable, exceeding even the unstable modes n = ±1 and n = ±3 that seed the breather. The red stars mark the maximum spectral component in each case.
FIG. 3. Spatio-temporal evolution of |ψ(1)| (left) and |ψ(2)| (right) for the exact third-order Akhmediev breather at β = 1.44.

FIG. 4. Temporal evolution of the discrete Fourier ampli- tudes |A(1) n | (left) and |A(2) n | (right) from t = −5 to t = 5 at β = 1.44. The horizontal dashed line marks the breather peak at t = 0.33, where the linearly stable n = ±2 harmonic becomes the dominant spectral component in both polariza- tions, exceeding the unstable modes n = ±1 and n = ±3 that seed the dynamics.
